summary:
The biggest news in this snapshot came out on Nov 9. The FDA is requiring every GLP-1 medicine, including Mounjaro and Zepbound, to add a warning about NAION, a rare eye condition, to the "warnings and precautions" section of the label. AP, CNN, NBC, CBS, WSJ, WaPo, STAT, Reuters and Medscape all covered it within hours. The FDA says NAION has been reported with all currently marketed GLP-1 products. It tells people to contact a provider right away if they get sudden vision loss in one eye (often on waking), blind spots, tunnel vision or colour changes.

Mainstream news is now peaking. Search from worried tirzepatide users will keep growing for weeks, and calm, label-based coverage is still thin. Because this is a label change rather than news, it fits Lane A: "Tirzepatide and Your Eyes: What the New Warning Says." Safety is caution: rare risk, no fear, no stopping advice, and don't confuse it with the temporary blurry vision that can come with blood sugar changes.

The second strong hook is a new randomized trial in Nature Medicine (Nov 9): 120 adults, tirzepatide alone vs tirzepatide plus resistance training. Strength dropped without training and went up substantially with it. That gives the stalled Strength video a fresh, adjacent angle without making another general protein video.

Also new and verified:
- Foundayo (orforglipron) ATTAIN-OSA results (AHA, JAMA): 712 people, AHI down up to 43.8% at 52 weeks.
- Retatrutide TRIUMPH-4 knee OA results at ACR.

ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17, REDEFINE 4: CagriSema vs tirzepatide) is the next scheduled spike. Thanksgiving (peak Nov 18–27) and the playbook's Lane A list keep their high scores: injection site, dehydration and sick days, alcohol, keeping results after stopping, burping and heartburn.

Rejected: anything about buying or online sources, plus semaglutide-only heart-failure data with a weak audience fit.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your eyes: the FDA's new class-wide NAION warning (Nov 9, 2026). Added to 'warnings and precautions' for all GLP-1 medicines, including Mounjaro and Zepbound; very rare; most common in adults 50 and over
candidates.angle: Calm, label-first explainer for people already on tirzepatide. What changed on the label and what NAION is, in plain words. How rare it is, and that the evidence has been strongest for semaglutide (the FDA says cases have been reported with all marketed GLP-1s). The exact warning signs the FDA lists: sudden vision loss in one eye, often on waking, blind spots, tunnel vision, colour changes. How that differs from the temporary blurry vision some people get when blood sugar changes quickly. Then what to do: call a provider right away if those signs appear, keep regular eye checks, especially with diabetes or eye disease, and bring questions to your prescriber. Never 'stop your shot'. The don't-stop line must be scoped: sudden vision loss means getting help right away. Long-form title idea: 'Tirzepatide and Your Eyes: The New Warning' (state-change thumbnail: worried → answered, no scary eye imagery). 08:00 Short: 'Tirzepatide and blurry vision: is this normal?'
candidates.predicted_peak: News peak 1–4 days; search from tirzepatide users stays high for 2–6 weeks
candidates.why_now: On Nov 9 the FDA required class-wide label changes. Every major US outlet ran it within hours, and international pickup (Korea, Australia) has started. Mainstream coverage is headline-driven ('incurable blindness', NY Post), so a calm, tirzepatide-specific, label-based explainer is the gap. It also fits the 'Is this normal?' body-worry format, our best Shorts format.

evidence.signal: The FDA requires Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy labels to add NAION to warnings and precautions. Cases have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 products.
Very rare; most common in adults 50 and over; can cause permanent vision loss. Warning signs: sudden loss in one eye on waking, blind spots, tunnel vision, colour changes.
FDA requires safety labeling updates. NAION causes sudden vision loss, with no proven treatment.
FDA tells GLP-1 makers to warn of potential vision loss.

evidence.source: PubMed, J Korean Med Sci review (Nov 2)
evidence.signal: Review of GLP-1 RA ocular safety and retinal outcomes, for background context

candidates.topic: Does lifting weights protect your muscle on tirzepatide? First RCT of resistance training with tirzepatide (Nature Medicine, Nov 9, 2026; 120 adults, 60 men and 60 postmenopausal women; 61 tirzepatide alone vs 59 tirzepatide plus supervised resistance training)
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide muscle loss: does lifting actually help?' Fresh randomized evidence: strength fell in the tirzepatide-only group and rose substantially with training. Use it as a 13:00 'fresh randomized result' Short. Use it as the refresh hook for the stalled Strength long-form (pinned comment, description quick answer, and a ▶ Watch next link from the Short's related-video setting). Keep exact arms, population and outcomes. Lean-mass figures must come from the paper itself. Not a single-trial long-form deep dive.
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days (UWA press release Nov 10; consumer health outlets follow)
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine on Nov 9, with a UWA press release a few hours ago. Fox News 'Ozempic users preserve muscle' coverage shows the mainstream appetite. Few creators have this trial yet. It sits right next to our Strength video, which needs a lift.

evidence.signal: First RCT of resistance exercise plus tirzepatide; 120 participants. Strength was compromised on tirzepatide alone and substantially increased with training.
'Resistance training key to maintaining muscle function during GLP-1 weight loss'
Mainstream interest: '6-minute daily habit could help Ozempic users preserve muscle'

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, alcohol and easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Shorts, each answering one fresh question, e.g. 'Tirzepatide at Thanksgiving: will I feel sick if I overeat?' or 'Will pie make the nausea worse?'. Each points to the Thanksgiving long-form via the related-video link. Avoid date words in evergreen copy.
candidates.why_now: 10 snapshots of steady acceleration (83→93). The holiday search peak is 8–17 days out, and the long-form is already being picked up by suggested video (17→83 min).

evidence.signal: Momentum rose steadily from 83 to 93
GLP-1 users reshaping food and drink habits, so interest in eating patterns stays high

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: is it normal? Redness, itching, small lumps; label rates given per dose vs placebo; when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Long-form at the top of the playbook: 'Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: Normal?' Give label rates per dose (6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 and 15 mg, vs about 2% placebo), never a pooled figure. Cover common causes, what helps, and the warning signs. Serious allergic reactions are post-marketing reports and need the scoped stop-and-get-help line. ▶ Watch next goes to Side Effects.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots, rising from 73 to 88. Its Short reached 232 views, our third-best body-worry Short. It's the playbook's #1 new Lane A topic.

evidence.signal: Injection-site Short: 232 views. Playbook ranks it #1 among new Lane A topics.
Class-wide label changes put the spotlight back on reading the label carefully

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4 regain, why it varies, and the habits linked to holding on (strength training, protein, plan with your prescriber)
candidates.angle: An adjacent follow-up to the Stopping video (8.44% CTR): 'After Tirzepatide: How People Keep Results'. Today's resistance-training RCT gives a fresh hook for the muscle and strength piece. SURMOUNT-4 numbers exactly as given in the notes. No stopping or tapering advice.
candidates.predicted_peak: Ongoing; rises again in January (New Year)
candidates.why_now: Stopping is our best Lane A start since Side Effects, and this is the closest unanswered next question. Medscape's Nov 7 coverage and new muscle data keep it fresh.

evidence.signal: Resistance training kept strength up during tirzepatide treatment; useful for the muscle piece of the maintenance story
Stopping long-form: 8.44% CTR and 143 min by day 3

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and dehydration on sick days: cold, flu or stomach bug; the label's acute kidney injury warning linked to vomiting and diarrhoea
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide Dehydration: Signs to Watch For'. Practical signs, why fluids matter more when you're eating less, the label's kidney warning, and checking cold medicines with a pharmacist. Help lines must cover all four markets. The new observational data on starting NSAIDs and GI bleeding can be one carefully hedged line ('ask a pharmacist about pain relievers'), never a headline.
candidates.predicted_peak: Seasonal: Nov–Feb (Northern Hemisphere illness season); Dec–Feb Australian heat
candidates.why_now: Playbook Lane A #2. Respiratory and stomach-bug season is starting in the US, UK and Canada, and summer is starting in Australia. Seen in several snapshots at 72–80.

evidence.source: PubMed, Am J Health Syst Pharm (Nov 5)
evidence.signal: Retrospective cohort: starting NSAIDs and GI bleeding risk in GLP-1 RA users (observational; one caveat line only)
'Prescribing GLP-1s? Consider These Medication Adjustments', so medication interactions are top of mind for clinicians

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol over the holidays: what the label says, plus the new DOM target trial emulation of semaglutide and tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes (Nov 3)
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide and Alcohol: What to Know' before office-party and holiday season. What the label and evidence say, why some people feel drinks differently, and why many say they want to drink less (observational, 'linked to'). The low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas. Never give a 'safe amount'.
candidates.why_now: Holiday drinking season is starting. Two snapshots at 80, plus the JAMA Psychiatry survey and the DOM emulation are recent. Playbook Lane A #4.

evidence.signal: Target trial emulation of semaglutide, tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes in T2D (observational)

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): full REDEFINE 4 results, CagriSema vs tirzepatide in adults with obesity (open-label, 84 weeks; topline about 23% with CagriSema, non-inferiority to tirzepatide not met)
candidates.angle: 13:00 head-to-head Short, tirzepatide first and in an obesity population: 'Tirzepatide vs CagriSema: what the full trial showed'. Randomized, open-label, with exact arms and timeframe. If the full data appear within 48 h, it qualifies as the playbook's allowed extra L2 news exception (randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide).
candidates.why_now: Scheduled conference spike 4–7 days out, already tracked in 3 snapshots. Tirzepatide-first head-to-heads earn 108–176 views on our Shorts.

evidence.signal: REDEFINE 4 full presentation expected at ObesityWeek Nov 14–17

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill for sleep apnea: ATTAIN-OSA phase 3 (AHA 2026, JAMA; 712 adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and obesity or overweight; AHI down by up to 43.8% without PAP and 27.5% with PAP at 52 weeks)
candidates.angle: 'GLP-1 pill and sleep apnea: what's confirmed?' Explain the results with both studies' numbers. Say it's not yet approved for OSA (Lilly plans to file by end of 2026). Tirzepatide is already approved for OSA in adults with obesity, and these are separate trials, not head-to-head. Keep tirzepatide in the title for search: 'Tirzepatide vs the new GLP-1 pill for sleep apnea: what's confirmed?'
candidates.why_now: Announced Nov 9 at AHA with JAMA publication. Covered by CNBC, STAT and Fierce, but few health creators have it yet.

evidence.signal: Foundayo significantly reduced OSA severity in Phase 3
Late-stage win paves the way for an FDA filing
Foundayo helped alleviate sleep apnea in studies

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: why it happens and what helps (slower stomach emptying, smaller meals, not lying down after eating)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide Burping and Heartburn: What Helps'. Label rates per dose vs placebo, practical habits, and when reflux needs a clinician. Holiday-meal timing helps it. ▶ Watch next goes to Side Effects.
candidates.predicted_peak: Ongoing; bump during Nov 20–Dec 31 holiday meals
candidates.why_now: Playbook Lane A #5. This side-effect question is next to the big three and no live video answers it. Holiday big meals make it more relevant.

evidence.signal: Listed as the next Lane A topic; side-effect neighbours earn most of their minutes from suggested video

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide, pregnancy and planning: the 'Ozempic baby' conversation (NPR, Nov 9), the new animal study on semaglutide in pregnancy, and the label's oral-contraceptive caution
candidates.angle: Calm Short: 'Tirzepatide and pregnancy: what the label says'. Animal data are not human results. Cover the label's advice on planning and contraception: oral pills 'may reduce the efficacy' for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase, so consider adding a barrier method. Talk to your prescriber before trying to conceive. ▶ Watch next goes to the Birth Control long-form.
candidates.why_now: Three independent signals in 24 h: the NPR Short Wave episode, the News-Medical animal study and Newswise 'Could Ozempic and Wegovy affect unborn babies?'. Our Birth Control long-form is already live to link to.

evidence.signal: 'An Ozempic baby boom? The GLP-1 pregnancy plot twist'
Animal study raises questions about semaglutide in pregnancy (animal data only)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis: TRIUMPH-4 full results at ACR 2026 (adults with obesity and knee OA; 68 weeks; average change in WOMAC pain score)
candidates.angle: 'Retatrutide knee pain trial: what's confirmed?' Describe the result as 'average change in pain score' vs placebo. Retatrutide is not approved, and online 'research' products aren't the trial drug. This counts as the week's single retatrutide-trial Short.
candidates.why_now: Presented at ACR on Nov 8, covered Nov 9 by Medscape, Everyday Health and Medical Xpress. Retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' angles perform for us (81–280).

evidence.signal: Retatrutide improves knee OA pain and physical function
Retatrutide reduces knee OA pain and body weight in patients with obesity

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the thyroid warning: what's confirmed? Endocrine Reviews review of preclinical and human data on GLP-1 medicines and thyroid cancer (Nov 6)
candidates.angle: With the NAION change putting labels in the news, a 'Tirzepatide thyroid warning: what does it actually mean?' Short. Rodent findings vs human data, who the label says shouldn't use it (MTC or MEN 2 history), and the neck symptoms to report.
candidates.predicted_peak: Ongoing; label-warning news lifts it over the next 1–2 weeks
candidates.why_now: A fresh authoritative review, plus heightened attention to GLP-1 label warnings after the Nov 9 FDA action.

evidence.signal: Review of preclinical and human data on GLP-1 RAs and thyroid cancer

candidates.topic: Gout and uric acid on GLP-1 medicines: systematic review and meta-analysis (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 8)
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide and gout: will it help?' Only if the meta-analysis includes tirzepatide data; otherwise frame it as 'GLP-1 medicines'. Report the pooled change in uric acid at the review's exact scope. Benefits beyond weight, positive but hedged.
candidates.why_now: A new meta-analysis with no consumer coverage yet. Gout has a large adult audience in the US, UK and Australia.

evidence.signal: Effects of GLP-1 RAs on hyperuricemia, serum uric acid and gout: SR/MA

candidates.topic: Semaglutide in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: Nature Medicine hemodynamic RCT and CAMEO-SEMA cardiac MRI substudy (Nov 8)
candidates.angle: Semaglutide-only evidence, so the title rules allow a semaglutide title. But the audience fit is narrow and it's a single trial. Hold as background for a future 'benefits beyond weight: heart' piece.
candidates.why_now: Two Nature Medicine papers; little consumer pickup.

evidence.signal: Placebo-controlled RCT of semaglutide hemodynamics in HFpEF with obesity

candidates.topic: REJECT: buying and online-source content (FDA warning on online weight-loss drugs with uncertain ingredients, WFTV Nov 9; 'where to buy' affiliate roundups, compounded and research-peptide platforms, 'natural GLP-1 alternative' supplements)
candidates.angle: Don't make content that points to any source. At most one gray-market Short a week, and only as a pure FDA-safety message with no sellers named. Better skipped this week given stronger topics.

evidence.signal: FDA warns against online weight-loss drugs containing uncertain ingredients
